descriptionMarkdown:
Unique items have no ordinary Requisition test. Each should be tied to a mission, inheritance, patron, theft, recovered 
vault, political bargain or equivalent campaign event. The examples below are templates for campaign-defining rewards 
rather than assumptions about what every high-level character owns.
Unique Item Availability Effect and Burden
Halo of Saint Varro Unique
Once per long rest as a bonus action, for 1 minute, you and allies within 15 
ft have advantage on fear and Corruption saves; you gain resistance to 
psychic and force damage. Burden: visible possession attracts 
Ecclesiarchal attention and expectations.
Heart-Key of the Red Vault Unique
Mechanicus interface. Once per long rest, treat one Technology check to 
unlock, disable or command a machine, security system or vehicle of DC 20 
or lower as a success. Against harder systems, make the check with 
advantage and add 1d10. Burden: multiple forge worlds claim it.
The First Oathstone Unique
Kin relic. Once per long rest, when a creature harms you or an ally within 30 
ft, name it oath-bound for 1 minute. Once each round when an ally hits that 
creature, that ally adds your proficiency bonus to the damage. Burden: 
abandoning the oath has serious cultural consequences.
The Veiled Eye Unique
Aeldari spirit-lens. Once per long rest as a bonus action, for 1 minute, you 
can see Invisible and Hidden creatures within 60 ft, cannot be Surprised, 
and your ranged attacks ignore Light Cover. Burden: The item carries a 
psychic echo noticeable to Aeldari and Warp-sensitive beings.
The Door That Would Not Break Unique
+2 AC; Ogryn only; counts as a Slab Shield and has no Speed penalty. If 
you do not move, up to two Small or Medium allies directly behind you have 
Full Cover. Once per long rest, when a weapon attack hits you, reduce that 
attack's damage to 0. Burden: it is enormous and impossible to conceal.
The Ghost's Coin Unique
Black-market data-sigil. Once per long rest, produce a convincing identity, 
access token or ownership record appropriate to the current settlement or 
institution; for one scene, gain advantage on Deception and Investigation 
checks that rely on it. Burden: every use risks attracting whoever originally 
issued the stolen credentials.
